question: Should OpenClaw adopt these four named hosting profiles and the public readiness-criterion plugin API as a supported core contract, rather than keeping readiness generic until the dependent layers are independently accepted?
rationale: The PR adds permanent configuration, environment, CLI, protocol, and plugin-SDK surfaces while its underlying readiness framework and core condition layers remain open; implementation quality alone cannot decide that product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor and stage the contract
options.body: Confirm the core API and profile direction, land or rebase the prerequisite readiness layers in an agreed order, and require the missing package-installed Docker evidence before merging profiles.

options.title: Accept one combined feature stack
options.body: Treat the branch as a single release-scoped readiness package and explicitly accept the larger review and upgrade surface.

options.title: Pause profile standardization
options.body: Keep generic readiness work separate and defer named hosting profiles until maintainers want a supported deployment-posture contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and stage the contract
recommendation.body: Confirm the core API and profile direction, land or rebase the prerequisite readiness layers in an agreed order, and require the missing package-installed Docker evidence before merging profiles.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor owns the submitted feature stack and can supply implementation context, while the final contract decision remains with repository maintainers.
